skill.name: ai-image-generation
skill.description: Generate AI images through the hosted Image Skill runtime using guided text-to-image and prompt-to-image workflows.
skill.summary: Hosted text-to-image generation for agents using the Image Skill CLI and API.
skill.author: danielgwilson

security_audit.summary: The audit found no prompt injection text, but the skill does instruct agents to run npm-based CLI commands and use a hosted image API. Several static hits were Markdown false positives, while the confirmed risks are external command execution, remote-provided command execution, hosted network dependency, and hidden agent state writes.

remediation.issue: Commands install and run image-skill@latest through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin npm package versions and require explicit user confirmation before running installation or generation commands.

remediation.issue: The skill asks agents to run data.next_command from guide output.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid executing service-provided command strings. Build commands locally from validated fields and display them for approval first.

remediation.issue: Global install commands use -g and -y for Codex skill state.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer workspace-scoped installation and document the persistent files changed before any global install.

remediation.issue: The workflow sends prompts and job data to a hosted API.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to include secrets or private images in prompts sent to the hosted service.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 uses Markdown inline code to name the image-skill runtime concepts. It does not instruct shell execution or interpolate untrusted input.
Line 28 tells agents to run data.next_command from the guide output when a flag is true. That is a real external command workflow controlled by tool output rather than a fixed local command.
Lines 32-34 contain an npx command that installs and runs image-skill@latest. Executing a latest npm package introduces supply-chain and network execution risk.
This range is the close of one Markdown code block and the start of a section. It does not contain an executable command beyond formatting markers.
Lines 38-40 include an npx image-skill@latest create command. The command runs external package code and contacts a hosted generation service.
This range contains Markdown formatting and prose before the install command block. The detected backticks here are not themselves shell execution.
Lines 46-48 contain an npx skills add command with global installation flags. It runs external npm code and modifies agent skill state.
This range is a Markdown fence close plus explanatory prose. The static pattern matched formatting, not an executable instruction in this span.
Lines 52-54 contain another npx skills add command. It executes external package code and can change global Codex skill configuration.
This finding points to Markdown closure and prose about writable targets. It does not itself include a command invocation.
Line 59 uses inline code to name HOME and CODEX_HOME paths. It is filesystem guidance, not external command execution.
Lines 62-67 provide shell commands that change HOME, create directories, and run npx skills add. This is executable setup that modifies agent state.
The range includes line 78, which instructs users to run image-skill feedback create --json for fallback reporting. It is a weaker command signal but still directs CLI execution.
Line 5 is homepage metadata for the skill. A documentation URL alone does not show data exfiltration or unsafe network behavior.
Line 6 points to documentation for the hosted service. It is a reference link, not an instruction to send user data.
Line 10 identifies the canonical skill URL. It supports documentation discovery and is not evidence of unauthorized network access by itself.
Line 11 declares a hosted API endpoint at api.image-skill.com. The skill depends on an external service, so prompts and job metadata may leave the local environment.
Line 73 is a documentation link to the shared skill contract. It is not an executable network request or data transfer.
Line 74 links to the LLM contract documentation. It is reference material and does not by itself create a network security issue.
Line 75 links to CLI contract documentation. This is static documentation, not proof of unsafe network behavior.
Line 76 lists the hosted API endpoint used by the skill. This confirms dependency on an external service for image generation.
Line 59 describes writes to hidden agent and Codex state directories. Modifying hidden agent configuration can persist beyond the current task.
Line 63 changes HOME to a hidden workspace directory. This is a real filesystem redirection that changes where tools read and write state.
Line 64 sets CODEX_HOME under a hidden directory. This can affect Codex profile state and persisted skill configuration.

content.user_title: Generate Images with Hosted AI Models
content.value_statement: Agents often need images without local models or provider accounts. This skill routes text-to-image work through a hosted Image Skill CLI and API.
actual_capabilities: Runs a guided no-spend image generation setup through the Image Skill CLI.
Creates hosted images from text prompts using model and cost parameters.
Supports durable hosted media URLs and recoverable generation jobs.
Documents installation through the skills CLI for Codex-compatible agents.
Points agents to shared skill, LLM, CLI, and hosted API contracts.
limitations: Requires network access to the hosted Image Skill service.
Uses npm and npx commands, which need user approval in restricted environments.
Generated image quality depends on available hosted models and service policy.
Media spend may occur when creation commands are approved.

use_cases.title: Create Concept Art
use_cases.description: Generate visual directions from short creative briefs without setting up a local image model.

use_cases.title: Produce Product Mockups
use_cases.description: Turn product descriptions into hosted image drafts with repeatable prompts and cost controls.

use_cases.title: Add Visual Assets
use_cases.description: Create article, documentation, or campaign images from agent-written prompts in one workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Begin With A Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-image-generation skill to start a no-spend guide for a simple product image prompt. Show me the planned command before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Draft Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-image-generation to create a hosted image of a compact field camera on a stainless workbench. Keep estimated cost low.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Prompt Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate three image prompt variants for a clean editorial hero image. Explain the intended composition and cost before creating images.

prompt_templates.title: Run A Controlled Production Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-image-generation for a production-ready product render. Specify model, intent, budget limit, prompt, and recovery details before running.

output_examples.input: Create a clean product image for a portable coffee grinder.
output_examples.output: The assistant prepares a hosted generation request, confirms the budget, and returns a durable image link with job details.

output_examples.input: Explore three styles for an article cover about urban gardens.
output_examples.output: The assistant drafts three visual prompt directions, explains tradeoffs, and can generate selected images after approval.

output_examples.input: Recover the previous generated image job.
output_examples.output: The assistant uses the hosted job record to locate prior media, receipts, and generation parameters.

best_practices: Review every generated command before allowing execution.
Set clear budget limits before creating hosted images.
Avoid private data, secrets, or confidential source images in prompts.
anti_patterns: Do not run service-provided commands without checking each argument.
Do not use unpinned latest packages in locked production workflows.
Do not assume hosted media is suitable for confidential work.

faq.question: Does this skill require a provider API key?
faq.answer: No. It uses the hosted Image Skill runtime instead of direct provider accounts.

faq.question: Can it run without network access?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow depends on hosted service endpoints and npm package access.

faq.question: Does it generate images directly inside the skill file?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides commands and contracts for using the hosted CLI and API.

faq.question: Can it control image generation costs?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented commands include estimated per-image cost limits and guide checks.

faq.question: Is it safe for confidential prompts?
faq.answer: Use caution. Prompts and job metadata may be sent to the hosted service.

faq.question: Which agents can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
